previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, diastolic dysfunction, and obstructive sleep apnea was admitted for lightheadedness and low blood pressure after taking her full regimen of antihypertensive medications. She reported chronic nausea worsened by eating, along with recent diarrhea and poor oral intake. Initial labs revealed acute kidney injury with creatinine rising to 3.2 mg/dL, attributed to pre-renal causes from hypotension. She received IV fluids, which resolved the renal dysfunction. Her blood pressure medications were adjusted—clonidine was discontinued due to symptomatic hypotension. An EGD showed a benign gastric polyp and a retained blue suture near the lower esophageal sphincter, with no evidence of H. pylori or gastritis. Citalopram was stopped due to possible contribution to nausea. Symptoms improved but nausea persisted with meals, prompting a recommendation for outpatient gastric emptying study. She was discharged on adjusted medications including pantoprazole and on-demand Zofran, with stable vital signs and normal kidney function.

constipation for four days, resolved with Dulcolax suppository, 
colace, and soap suds enema ___. GI was initially consulted

signed off the following day given they felt her symptoms were 
consistent with viral gastroenteritis. Abdominal CT on admission

nausea persisted, and she was unable to advance beyond clear 
liquids. GI was re-consulted on ___ and agreed with 
impression of possible gastroparesis.  Gastric emptying study 
showed gastroparesis.  High dose Ondansetron recommended per GI 
for diabetic gastroparesis.  She was able to tolerate staged 
full diet meals, she should go out with lactose free diet 
instructions.
